sentence: This project tries to find out how the collagen triple helix can twist and self-assemble into higher-order assemblies.
This project gets a scanning electron microscope that lets many laboratories study nanomaterials, fossils and biological samples.
The projects study the mechanisms of circadian clocks and cancer cell migration and design biosensors, antibacterial hydrogels and drug delivery systems.
This project studies whether increases in dissolved organic matter cause a lake regime shift through low dissolved oxygen in bottom waters.
This project works to help robots see real-world work the way human workers do, using insights into how people think and behave.
This project builds predictive models and feedback regulators that help genetic circuits made with CRISPR work reliably when parts compete for cellular resources.
This project designs doped semiconducting polymers that stay stable when ions repeatedly move into them, using computer simulations and machine learning.
This project tries to find out how electrical charges and water change the atomic structure of metal oxide surfaces.
This project builds a robot system for field-based labs and studies whether it supports collaborative problem-solving skills for remote and residential learners.
This project tries to find out which sources, such as dust, monsoon rains and sediments, supply trace metals and nutrients to ocean waters.
This project uses mass spectrometry to identify high molecular weight disinfection byproducts that form when chlorine reacts with dissolved organic matter in water.
This project uses theory to study how charge moves through quantum electronic devices and how energy relaxation affects superconducting devices.
This project studies the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of random matrices with dependent entries, which arise in random networks, statistical genetics and neural networks.
This project uses stem cells to build engineered cardiac tissues and studies how neurons connect to heart cells and change the beat rate.
This project studies how gluons give the proton its mass, spin and structure, using lattice Quantum Chromodynamics, quantum computing and machine learning.
This project acquires a system that coats surfaces with ultra-thin, uniform layers to improve devices such as perovskite-based solar cells and rechargeable batteries.
